verdict.line: You blow K'Sante out before level 6 with Fury-fueled W/E all-ins, but lose the identity of the lane once he hits R and starts scaling into items.

brief.thesis: K'Sante has no real kill pressure before level 6 outside of landing his long-cooldown W stun, while Renekton's Fury system turns W (Ruthless Predator) and E (Slice and Dice) into a full stun-lock all-in the moment his Fury bar crosses 50. Past level 6, K'Sante's All Out lets him knock you through walls and dash in with bonus damage and healing, which flips the trade math even though he's trading his own defenses to do it.

theirWindow.what: Once he has All Out, he can knock you back through terrain and then dash in as a transformed, higher-damage version of himself, gaining healing along the way. He's giving up defenses to do this, so if you survive the initial knockback you can win the follow-up fight - just don't get caught with your back to a wall or brush edge.

yourWindow.what: When your Fury is above 50 and both W and E are up, commit. Empowered W hits three times, destroys any shield he has up, and stuns for 1.5 seconds instead of 0.75 - that alone denies his Footwork shield. Chain empowered E's armor reduction right after to keep the damage rolling before his 14-10s W or 10-8s E come back.

powerCurve.note: Neither side has a real kill threat yet
Fury-capped W/E all-in window is open
All Out threatens burst through walls

start.why: Sustain through his early Q poke while you wait to hit your Fury-capped all-in levels.

boots.why: Cuts down his auto-attacks and Q line-strike poke, which is all the damage he has before 6.

core.why: Gives you the burst and attack speed to actually close out kills during your pre-6 window instead of just poking.
Stacking armor shred layers on top of your own E's armor reduction, keeping your damage relevant as he stacks resistances.
The extra health and damage reduction keeps you alive through his All Out burst once he starts scaling past you.

situational.when: he keeps resetting your all-ins by popping Footwork's shield
his All Out is threatening to one-shot you in skirmishes
his team stacks hard CC on top of his stuns

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the extended trades your W/E combo forces and keeps ramping through the sustained fighting this matchup demands.

summoners.why: You want to close out kills during your levels 3-5 all-in window before his level 6 flips the matchup, and Ignite guarantees the kill through his Footwork shield.

playing.title: Stack Fury before diving
playing.detail: Farm with autos and Q resets on cannon waves to get your Fury bar above 50 before you commit, since your empowered W's third hit, shield-destroy, and 1.5s stun only trigger above that threshold.

playing.title: Punish his pre-6 approaches
playing.detail: He has no kill pressure before level 6 outside landing his W (Path Maker) charge-dash stun. Sidestep the charge-up and punish with your E while his W sits on its 14-10s cooldown.

playing.title: Track his Q stacks
playing.detail: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes he fires a pull shockwave that yanks you in. Don't sit at the edge of his Q range letting him farm free stacks off you.

playing.title: Bait Footwork before committing
playing.detail: Poke out his E shield with a Q before you throw your full W/E combo, or just rely on empowered W's third hit to strip the shield outright.

playing.title: Respect walls after his 6
playing.detail: Once he hits level 6, avoid fighting with your back to a wall or brush edge - All Out can knock you through terrain and follow you in with bonus damage and healing.

playing.title: Sequence W into E
playing.detail: Land the stun first, then use empowered E's armor reduction to soften him for the rest of the trade rather than opening with E.

playing.title: Watch his cooldowns tighten late
playing.detail: By level 11 his W drops to 11s and E to 8.5s, so his disengage comes back much faster than it did early - don't overextend expecting the same openings you had at level 5.

brief.patchCaveat: Ability cooldowns and effects above are taken directly from current game text. Item and rune names can drift patch to patch - verify the exact Trinity Force/Black Cleaver/Conqueror builds are still live before locking in, but the underlying early-favoured, late-scaling shape of this matchup has held across recent patches.
